spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The unit builds a single coordinate system for the later closure criterion. The fractional-part kernel is placed in Lp spaces, dilation is made into a bounded operator, B(g) records the span of integer dilates, and the Mellin transform turns suitable functions into analytic objects on the critical strip. What matters is not any one definition but their compatibility: a dilation-generated approximation problem is prepared for transform-side analysis.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source defines C0 and its compact-support and differentiable subspaces, chi on (0,1], rho_1(x)=rho(1/x), the bounded dilations K_lambda f(x)=f(lambda x), the linear hull B(g) of K_n g for positive integers n, and the Mellin transform. It states rho_1 is in Lp for p>1 and that membership of f in every Lp with 1<p<infinity gives absolute, locally uniform Mellin convergence and analyticity for 0<Re(s)<1.
directed.conceptual_reading: These definitions align three structures: approximation in function space, symmetry under dilation, and analytic coordinates in the Mellin variable. B(g) deliberately forgets the particular coefficients of an approximant while preserving reachability from g by the permitted integer dilations.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The Mellin transform is the natural bridge because scaling in the original variable has a simple transform-side action; B(g) packages the orbit of a kernel under the dilations that will drive the closure problem.
directed.boundary_or_failure: No closure theorem or zeta identity is proved in this span. Integer dilates define B(g), even though K_lambda is defined for every positive lambda, and the analytic-strip claim requires the stated all-p integrability hypothesis.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The necessity proof does not rebuild an approximation for every good kernel. It transports the classical Nyman-Beurling approximants through one bounded dilation-invariant operator. Commutation carries each dilate of rho_1 to the corresponding dilate of P f, the factorization carries -chi to f, and L2 boundedness carries convergence. The result is a reusable transfer principle rather than a new Gramian calculation.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Assuming RH, Theorem 1.1 provides h_n in B(rho_1) with h_n approaching -chi in L2. For a good kernel f, the proof sets H_n=T_{f'}h_n. Since T_{f'} commutes with dilations and P f=T_{f'}rho_1, each H_n lies in B(P f). Because T_{f'}chi=-f and T_{f'} is bounded on L2, H_n converges to f, proving f belongs to the L2 closure of B(P f).
directed.conceptual_reading: The proof identifies an intertwiner that preserves all structure relevant to the closure statement: the generating orbit, its linear combinations, and its limit. The difficult classical result is therefore inherited by an entire kernel class.
directed.representation_or_bridge: T_{f'} is the bridge from the base pair (rho_1,-chi) to (P f,f). Dilation equivariance maps the spans, factorization maps the target, and boundedness maps convergence.
directed.boundary_or_failure: This proves only the RH-conditioned necessity direction and relies on f being good so the identities and L2 bound apply. An unbounded or non-equivariant map would not preserve the closure argument.
directed.uncertainty: Coefficient indices, signs, and closure typography need PDF checking, but the intertwining proof is fully legible at the structural level.

supported: The candidate accurately traces h_n approaching -chi, applies T_{f'} to obtain H_n, uses dilation commutation and P f=T_{f'}rho_1 to land in B(P f), and uses L2 boundedness plus T_{f'}chi=-f to preserve convergence.
It correctly limits the conclusion to the RH-conditioned necessity direction for good kernels.
inference: Interpreting T_{f'} as an intertwiner preserving the generating orbit, finite linear combinations, and the relevant limit is directly supported by the proof.
unsupported_or_imported: The sentence that an unbounded or non-equivariant map would not preserve the closure argument is too categorical: such a map could preserve this particular sequence or span by other means; the source only shows that boundedness and equivariance make the displayed proof work.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The reverse direction needs to evaluate Mellin transforms at a fixed zeta zero, but raw L2 convergence does not make point evaluation continuous on an unbounded domain. The invariant difference V=I-2K_2 creates a mean-zero compactly supported kernel F and transformed approximants with one common bounded support. Muntz's formula kills each approximant's Mellin value, while Cauchy-Schwarz on that bounded interval passes the zero through the L2 limit; the dilation factor then returns the conclusion from F-hat to f-hat.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Let f be a compactly supported good kernel in the L2 closure of B(P f), and fix a zeta zero s with 1/2<Re(s)<1. From approximants h_n->f, the proof applies V=I-2K_2, defining F=Vf and H_n=Vh_n. Invariance puts H_n in B(P F), L2 continuity gives H_n->F, and compact support plus zero mean makes P F and all H_n vanish beyond a common bound A. Muntz's formula gives H_n-hat(s)=0. Cauchy-Schwarz on (0,A), where x^{s-1} is square integrable, then gives F-hat(s)=0; the displayed dilation relation between F-hat and f-hat yields f-hat(s)=0.
directed.conceptual_reading: V is a compactification-by-cancellation device. It preserves the dilation-span structure while adding the mean-zero condition that removes the tail of P F. This converts a discontinuous global point-evaluation problem into a bounded-interval continuous functional on L2.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge has three linked parts: the invariant operator V transports the closure, Muntz's formula converts a zeta zero into vanishing Mellin values of the approximants, and bounded support allows Hilbert-space convergence to pass that vanishing to the limit.
directed.boundary_or_failure: Compact support, mean cancellation, the common support bound, and Re(s)>1/2 are all essential to the stated Cauchy-Schwarz passage. Without them, L2 convergence alone would not justify Mellin evaluation. The proof establishes zero-set inclusion, not RH unless a separate nonvanishing condition on f-hat is available.
directed.uncertainty: The extraction compresses the exponent in the final factor and damages some support wording. The mechanism and logical dependencies are clear, but V's exact transform factor and display signs require the PDF.

supported: The candidate accurately traces V=I-2K_2, F=Vf, H_n=Vh_n, preservation of span structure and L2 convergence, zero mean, the common tail cutoff, Muntz vanishing at a fixed zeta zero, and the bounded-interval Cauchy-Schwarz passage.
It correctly limits the conclusion to zero-set inclusion unless f-hat is separately nonvanishing and preserves the essential range Re(s)>1/2.
inference: Viewing the bounded-support Mellin functional as continuous on L2(0,A), while global L2 convergence alone is insufficient, is a sound explanation of why the common cutoff matters.
unsupported_or_imported: Calling V a compactification device is imprecise: f is compactly supported by hypothesis and V preserves that support property while imposing mean cancellation; the cancellation is what makes P F, and hence its integer dilates, have a common tail cutoff.
